title: A triacontanuclear [Zn12Dy18] cluster: a ring of [Dy4] cubes

synthesis.procedure: Zn(OAc)2·2H2O, Dy(NO3)3·5H2O, 2-amino-isobutyric acid (aibH), and salicylaldehyde (salH) were combined in methanol with excess triethylamine. The mixture was transferred to a 23 mL Teflon-lined autoclave and held at 95 °C for 12 h. It was cooled slowly to room temperature at 10 °C h−1. Pale-yellow rod-like crystals were collected by filtration, washed with diethyl ether, and dried in air.
synthesis.temperature: 95 °C; subsequently cooled to room temperature at 10 °C h−1
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Slow cooling yielded pale-yellow rod-like crystals, which were filtered, washed with diethyl ether, and dried in air.

properties.summary: The cluster shows frequency-dependent out-of-phase ac susceptibility below approximately 4.5 K, indicating slow magnetic relaxation and possible single-molecule-magnet behavior. The authors caution that the decrease in χMT on cooling does not by itself establish antiferromagnetic interactions.

measurements.name: χMT
measurements.conditions: Room temperature; applied dc field 0.1 T

measurements.name: Curie–Weiss temperature
measurements.conditions: Qualitative fit of susceptibility data in the 50–300 K range

measurements.name: Frequency-dependent out-of-phase ac susceptibility
measurements.conditions: 3.5 G oscillating field; zero static dc field

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The discrete [Zn12Dy18] metallic core contains three pairs of corner-sharing [Dy4(OH)4] cubes arranged in a ring. Zinc centers and bridging ligands connect the cube pairs into the larger cluster.
